name: Al-Ḥāqqah
meaning: The Inevitable Reality or The Sure Truth (Al-Haqqah)
revelation_details: Makkan (Revealed during the early-to-middle Makkan period, a time of intense confrontation over the reality of Resurrection and the authenticity of Divine Revelation)
core_theme: The absolute certainty of Resurrection and Judgment Day (Al-Haqqah), the historical destruction of rebellious nations who denied accountability, the precise events of Judgment Day (the Trumpet, the Eight Angels, the distribution of Books), and the divine vindication of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an against slander.
name_origin:
The Surah derives its name, Al-Haqqah, directly from its striking opening verses:

• "The Inevitable Reality - What is the Inevitable Reality? And what can make you know what is the Inevitable Reality?"* (Verses 1-3)

Linguistic and Theological Significance

• Al-Haqqah (The Inevitable Reality): Derived from the root ha-qqa (truth, certainty, obligation). Judgment Day is called Al-Haqqah because it is guaranteed to occur beyond doubt, because on that Day all hidden truths (Haqq) will be made manifest, and because everyone will receive their true, deserved recompense.
• The Tripartite Repetition: Opening with three consecutive questions regarding Al-Haqqah creates atmospheric awe (Tahwil), alerting the listener to a catastrophic and undeniable event that transcends human imagination.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Inevitable Reality and the Destruction of Historical Rebels

points.label: Denial by Past Nations
points.detail: Both the ancient tribes of Thamud and 'Ad rejected this striking calamity (Al-Qari'ah).

points.label: The Annihilation of Thamud
points.detail: Thamud was utterly destroyed by an overpowering, violent noise and storm (At-Taghiyah).

points.label: The Continuous Fury Unleashed on 'Ad
points.detail: The tribe of 'Ad was destroyed by a furious, roaring, relentless wind that Allah unleashed upon them for seven nights and eight continuous days.

points.label: Visualizing Their Destruction
points.detail: If one were present, they would have seen the people lying dead and prone across the land like hollow, uprooted trunks of date palm trees (A'jazu Nakhlin Khawiyah). Allah asks: "Do you see any remnant (Baqiyah) left of them today?

points.label: The Arrogance of Pharaoh and His Contemporaries
points.detail: Pharaoh, the corrupt generations before him, and the overturned cities of Sodom and Gomorrah (Al-Mu'tafikāt) persistently committed grave, systemic sins.

points.label: The Consequence of Disobeying Messengers
points.detail: They defied the messenger sent by their Lord, so Allah seized them with an ever-escalating, suffocating grip (Akhdhatan Rabiyah).

points.label: The Great Flood and the Ark
points.detail: When the floodwaters rose out of bounds during the era of Prophet Nuh (Noah), Allah safely carried human ancestors inside the floating Ark.

points.label: The Purpose of Historical Memory
points.detail: Allah preserved this miraculous survival so that it would serve as a perpetual reminder and warning, to be heard, understood, and retained by "conscious and attentive ears" (Udhnun Wa'iyah).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Surah Al-Haqqah begins with a dramatic, repetitive declaration of the Day of Judgment, followed by historical case studies of arrogant civilizations that defied divine warnings:
• The Inescapable Reality (Al-Haqqah): The Surah opens with three sharp, rhetorical questions: "Al-Haqqah (The Inevitable Reality)! What is Al-Haqqah? And what will make you realize what Al-Haqqah is?" - emphasizing the absolute certainty and awe-inspiring gravity of Judgment Day.
• Denial by Past Nations: Both the ancient tribes of Thamud and 'Ad rejected this striking calamity (Al-Qari'ah).
• The Annihilation of Thamud: Thamud was utterly destroyed by an overpowering, violent noise and storm (At-Taghiyah).
• The Continuous Fury Unleashed on 'Ad: The tribe of 'Ad was destroyed by a furious, roaring, relentless wind that Allah unleashed upon them for seven nights and eight continuous days.
• Visualizing Their Destruction: If one were present, they would have seen the people lying dead and prone across the land like hollow, uprooted trunks of date palm trees (A'jazu Nakhlin Khawiyah). Allah asks: "Do you see any remnant (Baqiyah) left of them today?"
• The Arrogance of Pharaoh and His Contemporaries: Pharaoh, the corrupt generations before him, and the overturned cities of Sodom and Gomorrah (Al-Mu'tafikāt) persistently committed grave, systemic sins.
• The Consequence of Disobeying Messengers: They defied the messenger sent by their Lord, so Allah seized them with an ever-escalating, suffocating grip (Akhdhatan Rabiyah).
• The Great Flood and the Ark: When the floodwaters rose out of bounds during the era of Prophet Nuh (Noah), Allah safely carried human ancestors inside the floating Ark.
• The Purpose of Historical Memory: Allah preserved this miraculous survival so that it would serve as a perpetual reminder and warning, to be heard, understood, and retained by "conscious and attentive ears" (Udhnun Wa'iyah).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The opening repetition of Al-Haqqah - from the root meaning "truth" or "that which inevitably comes to pass" - serves as an intellectual wake-up call. Human beings naturally drift into routine, mistaking the stability of daily life for permanence. By naming Judgment Day Al-Haqqah, Allah reminds us that truth is not subjective; reality will eventually break through all human illusions and denials.
The historical survey in verses 4-12 illustrates a universal law of history: moral arrogance leads to physical destruction. The imagery of the people of 'Ad - once towering giants proud of their physical strength - lying scattered like "hollow palm trunks" shows how helpless human power becomes when it opposes divine law.
Notice the phrase in verse 12: "that retaining ears might remember it." History is not merely a collection of dates and ruins; it is a spiritual textbook. The difference between those who learn from history and those who repeat its mistakes lies in the willingness to cultivate an "attentive ear" (Udhnun Wa'iyah) - a mind willing to listen, reflect, and reform before crisis strikes.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Cosmic Upheaval and the Day of Absolute Unveiling

points.label: The Single Blast
points.detail: The cosmic end begins when the Trumpet (As-Soor) is blown with a single, decisive blast.

points.label: The Pulverization of Earth and Mountains
points.detail: The earth and all its mountain ranges will be lifted from their foundations and crushed against one another with a single, catastrophic blow (Dakkatan Wahidah).

points.label: The Occurrence of the Event
points.detail: On that terrifying Day, the Great Event (Al-Waqi'ah) will take place.

points.label: The Flimsy Sky
points.detail: The sky will split wide open, rendered frail, torn, and unstable (Wahiyah).

points.label: Angels at the Cosmic Edges
points.detail: Angels will stand around the borders and edges of the unraveling heavens.

points.label: The Bearing of the Throne
points.detail: On that Day, eight mighty angels will carry the Throne ('Arsh) of your Lord above them.

points.label: The Day of Absolute Unveiling
points.detail: Humanity will be marched forward for presentation and judgment: "On that Day you will be exhibited; not a single secret of yours will remain hidden." (La Takhfa Minkum Khafiyah).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah describes the physical dismantling of the cosmos on Judgment Day, leading up to the complete exposure of human deeds before the divine throne:
• The Single Blast: The cosmic end begins when the Trumpet (As-Soor) is blown with a single, decisive blast.
• The Pulverization of Earth and Mountains: The earth and all its mountain ranges will be lifted from their foundations and crushed against one another with a single, catastrophic blow (Dakkatan Wahidah).
• The Occurrence of the Event: On that terrifying Day, the Great Event (Al-Waqi'ah) will take place.
• The Flimsy Sky: The sky will split wide open, rendered frail, torn, and unstable (Wahiyah).
• Angels at the Cosmic Edges: Angels will stand around the borders and edges of the unraveling heavens.
• The Bearing of the Throne: On that Day, eight mighty angels will carry the Throne ('Arsh) of your Lord above them.
• The Day of Absolute Unveiling: Humanity will be marched forward for presentation and judgment: "On that Day you will be exhibited; not a single secret of yours will remain hidden." (La Takhfa Minkum Khafiyah).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
This passage contrasts the current solidity of our world with its ultimate fragility. Mountains - the very symbol of permanence on Earth - will be reduced to dust in a single crush. The sky, which appears vast and impenetrable, will hang like torn fabric. This cosmic deconstruction reminds us that the physical environment is merely a temporary stage built for human moral trial.
However, the psychological climax of this section occurs in verse 18: "Not a single secret of yours will remain hidden." In this world, people excel at managing reputations, masking motives, and hiding personal vices behind social status or pleasant demeanor. On the Day of Al-Haqqah, all privacy filters are removed. Secrets stored in hearts, private browsing histories, hidden financial dealings, and silent betrayals will be fully displayed. True wisdom means auditing our lives today so that our public reality on that Day is a source of honor rather than shame.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Triumph of the Righteous: Receiving the Record in the Right Hand

points.label: The Jubilant Announcement
points.detail: The person who is handed their record of deeds in their right hand will be so overcome with happiness that they will call out to everyone around them: "Here! Read my record!" (Ha'umu Iqra'oo Kitabiyah!).

points.label: The Foundation of Success
points.detail: They explain the secret to their success: "Indeed, I was certain in my earthly life that I would eventually meet my account!" (Innee Dhanantu Annee Mulaqin Hisabiyah).

points.label: An Elevated Life
points.detail: As a result, this person will enjoy a blissful, highly satisfied life (Fee 'Eeshatin Radiyah).

points.label: The Description of Paradise
points.detail: They will reside in an exalted, lofty Garden (Jannatin 'Aliyah).

points.label: Accessibility of Reward
points.detail: Its clusters of ripe fruit will hang low, within effortless reach (Qutoofuha Daniyah).

points.label: The Divine Welcoming Address
points.detail: They will be warmly invited: "Eat and drink delightfully and with complete peace of mind, as a reward for the good deeds you sent ahead in the days gone by!

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah depicts the overwhelming joy and eternal reward of those who pass the divine accounting, highlighting their mindset during earthly life:
• The Jubilant Announcement: The person who is handed their record of deeds in their right hand will be so overcome with happiness that they will call out to everyone around them: "Here! Read my record!" (Ha'umu Iqra'oo Kitabiyah!).
• The Foundation of Success: They explain the secret to their success: "Indeed, I was certain in my earthly life that I would eventually meet my account!" (Innee Dhanantu Annee Mulaqin Hisabiyah).
• An Elevated Life: As a result, this person will enjoy a blissful, highly satisfied life (Fee 'Eeshatin Radiyah).
• The Description of Paradise: They will reside in an exalted, lofty Garden (Jannatin 'Aliyah).
• Accessibility of Reward: Its clusters of ripe fruit will hang low, within effortless reach (Qutoofuha Daniyah).
• The Divine Welcoming Address: They will be warmly invited: "Eat and drink delightfully and with complete peace of mind, as a reward for the good deeds you sent ahead in the days gone by!
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The scene of the successful believer receiving their record in their right hand is one of the most heartwarming moments in scripture. The Arabic phrase Ha'umu Iqra'oo Kitabiyah! captures the ecstatic relief of a student who receives top marks after years of grueling study and cannot wait to show their transcript to family and friends.
Verse 20 reveals the psychological key to living a righteous life: a continuous, practical awareness of accountability (Hisab). The word Dhanantu here signifies deep, unshakable conviction rather than mere guesswork. The person who lives with the conscious awareness that every word, financial transaction, and private action will be reviewed does not live a life of perfection, but one of constant self-correction and repentance.
Notice also the phrasing in verse 24: "for what you sent ahead in the days gone by." This life is an investment window. Every act of patience, charity, truthfulness, and restraint is capital transferred ahead to the Afterlife, waiting to be returned as eternal joy.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Agony of the Lost: Receiving the Record in the Left Hand and Dual Failures

points.label: The Despair of the Lost
points.detail: The person who receives their record of deeds in their left hand will cry out in agony: "Oh, I wish I had never been given my record,

points.label: Wishing for Extinction
points.detail: And that I had never known what my accounting was!

points.label: Regret Over Death
points.detail: Oh, I wish that my death had been the permanent end of my existence!" (Ya Laytaha Kanatil-Qadiyah).

points.label: The Futility of Worldly Assets
points.detail: They realize the absolute worthlessness of their past status: "My wealth has not availed me at all!" (Ma A'na 'Annee Maliyah).

points.label: The Loss of Power
points.detail: My power, authority, and arguments have completely vanished from me!" (Halaka 'Annee Sultaniyah).

points.label: The Divine Sentence
points.detail: The command will issue from the Sovereign: "Seize him and shackle him!

points.label: Cast into the Fire
points.detail: Then cast him into the blazing Hellfire,

points.label: Bound in Chains
points.detail: Then tie him up in a chain whose length is seventy cubits!

points.label: The First Root Cause of Ruin
points.detail: Allah explains the double spiritual failure that led to this fate: First, "Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Most Great,

points.label: The Second Root Cause of Ruin
points.detail: Second, "Nor did he urge or encourage the feeding of the poor." (Wa La Yahuddu 'Ala Ta'amil-Miskeen).

points.label: Total Isolation
points.detail: Consequently, on that Day, he will have no close friend or defender to help him,

points.label: The Wretched Provision
points.detail: Nor any food except Ghisleen - a foul, painful discharge from the wounds of the damned,

points.label: The Exclusive Consumer
points.detail: Which no one will eat except the persistent, unrepentant sinners (Al-Khati'oon).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
In stark contrast, Allah details the terrifying regret, public humiliation, and cosmic condemnation of those who reject divine truth and neglect human compassion:
• The Despair of the Lost: The person who receives their record of deeds in their left hand will cry out in agony: "Oh, I wish I had never been given my record,"
• Wishing for Extinction: "And that I had never known what my accounting was!"
• Regret Over Death: "Oh, I wish that my death had been the permanent end of my existence!" (Ya Laytaha Kanatil-Qadiyah).
• The Futility of Worldly Assets: They realize the absolute worthlessness of their past status: "My wealth has not availed me at all!" (Ma A'na 'Annee Maliyah).
• The Loss of Power: "My power, authority, and arguments have completely vanished from me!" (Halaka 'Annee Sultaniyah).
• The Divine Sentence: The command will issue from the Sovereign: "Seize him and shackle him!"
• Cast into the Fire: "Then cast him into the blazing Hellfire,"
• Bound in Chains: "Then tie him up in a chain whose length is seventy cubits!"
• The First Root Cause of Ruin: Allah explains the double spiritual failure that led to this fate: First, "Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Most Great,"
• The Second Root Cause of Ruin: Second, "Nor did he urge or encourage the feeding of the poor." (Wa La Yahuddu 'Ala Ta'amil-Miskeen).
• Total Isolation: Consequently, on that Day, he will have no close friend or defender to help him,
• The Wretched Provision: Nor any food except Ghisleen - a foul, painful discharge from the wounds of the damned,
• The Exclusive Consumer: Which no one will eat except the persistent, unrepentant sinners (Al-Khati'oon).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The monologue of the person who receives their book in their left hand (verses 25-29) is a masterclass in ultimate regret. In this world, wealth (Mal) and authority (Sultan) are the two primary metrics by which humans measure success and construct feelings of invincibility. On Judgment Day, both dissolve into utter uselessness. The realization that one's status was an empty illusion produces a desire for total non-existence ("Oh, I wish death had ended everything!").
Crucially, verses 33-34 diagnose the two pillars of human damnation, establishing a core Quranic doctrine:
1. A broken relationship with the Creator: Refusing to believe in Allah, the Most Great (La Yu'minu Billahil-'Adheem).
2. A broken relationship with Creation: Refusing to encourage or participate in feeding the hungry (La Yahuddu 'Ala Ta'amil-Miskeen).
Notice that verse 34 does not merely condemn those who do not feed the poor; it explicitly condemns those who do not even urge or advocate for feeding the poor (La Yahuddu). Faith in God is incomplete if it does not produce active empathy, social justice, and systematic care for the vulnerable. Spiritual arrogance paired with indifference to human suffering leads directly to the terrible isolation described at the end of the passage.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Absolute Integrity of Revelation, the Divine Guarantee, and Haqqul-Yaqeen

points.label: The Cosmic Oath
points.detail: Allah swears a grand oath: "So I swear by what you see, and by what you do not see..." (Fa-La Uqsimu Bima Tubsiroon, Wa Ma La Tubsiroon).

points.label: The Dignified Transmission
points.detail: The Quran is indeed the spoken word conveyed by a noble, honorable Messenger [Gabriel / Muhammad (pbuh)].

points.label: Refutation of Poetry
points.detail: It is definitively not the word of a poet (Sha'ir) - how little faith you possess!

points.label: Refutation of Soothsayer Claims
points.detail: Nor is it the word of a fortune-teller or soothsayer (Kahin) - how little you reflect!

points.label: The True Origin
points.detail: It is a direct revelation sent down gradually from the Lord of all the worlds (Tanzeelum min Rabbil-'Alameen).

points.label: The Hypothetical Warning
points.detail: Allah presents an intense hypothetical scenario to prove the Prophet's integrity: "And if he [Muhammad] had fabricated any false sayings against Us,

points.label: Immediate Divine Retribution
points.detail: We would have surely seized him by his right hand,

points.label: Severing the Aorta
points.detail: And We would have severed his life-vein [aorta - Al-Wateen]!

points.label: Human Helplessness
points.detail: And not one of you could have shielded him or prevented Us from doing so!

points.label: A Reminder for the Mindful
points.detail: Indeed, this Quran is an eternal guidance and reminder for those who maintain God-consciousness (Muttaqeen).

points.label: Omniscient Awareness of Skeptics
points.detail: Allah acknowledges human stubbornness: "And indeed, We know that among you are those who deny it.

points.label: Source of Agony for Deniers
points.detail: On Judgment Day, this revelation will be a cause of deep grief, intense regret, and anguish (Hasrah) for those who rejected it.

points.label: The Absolute Truth
points.detail: Indeed, this Quran is the absolute, undisputed truth of certainty (Haqqul-Yaqeen).

points.label: The Concluding Command
points.detail: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great!" (Fa-Sabbih Bismi Rabbikal-'Adheem).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
The Surah concludes with a solemn divine oath affirming the origin and authenticity of the Quran, refuting false claims made against the Prophet (pbuh), and declaring the ultimate certainty of revelation:
• The Cosmic Oath: Allah swears a grand oath: "So I swear by what you see, and by what you do not see..." (Fa-La Uqsimu Bima Tubsiroon, Wa Ma La Tubsiroon).
• The Dignified Transmission: The Quran is indeed the spoken word conveyed by a noble, honorable Messenger [Gabriel / Muhammad (pbuh)].
• Refutation of Poetry: It is definitively not the word of a poet (Sha'ir) - how little faith you possess!
• Refutation of Soothsayer Claims: Nor is it the word of a fortune-teller or soothsayer (Kahin) - how little you reflect!
• The True Origin: It is a direct revelation sent down gradually from the Lord of all the worlds (Tanzeelum min Rabbil-'Alameen).
• The Hypothetical Warning: Allah presents an intense hypothetical scenario to prove the Prophet's integrity: "And if he [Muhammad] had fabricated any false sayings against Us,"
• Immediate Divine Retribution: "We would have surely seized him by his right hand,"
• Severing the Aorta: "And We would have severed his life-vein [aorta - Al-Wateen]!"
• Human Helplessness: "And not one of you could have shielded him or prevented Us from doing so!"
• A Reminder for the Mindful: Indeed, this Quran is an eternal guidance and reminder for those who maintain God-consciousness (Muttaqeen).
• Omniscient Awareness of Skeptics: Allah acknowledges human stubbornness: "And indeed, We know that among you are those who deny it."
• Source of Agony for Deniers: On Judgment Day, this revelation will be a cause of deep grief, intense regret, and anguish (Hasrah) for those who rejected it.
• The Absolute Truth: Indeed, this Quran is the absolute, undisputed truth of certainty (Haqqul-Yaqeen).
• The Concluding Command: "So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great!" (Fa-Sabbih Bismi Rabbikal-'Adheem).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The oath in verses 38-39 encompasses the entire realm of existence: everything we can perceive (Bima Tubsiroon) and everything hidden from our senses (Wa Ma La Tubsiroon). By swearing by all of reality, Allah emphasizes that the Quran is not an isolated human text, but a message woven into the very structure of the universe.
Verses 44-47 contain one of the most formidable warnings in all of scripture regarding religious integrity. To prove to the critics of Makkah that Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was not altering or inventing divine message for personal gain, Allah declares that if even His beloved Messenger were to forge a single sentence in God's name, divine justice would strike instantly by severing his aorta (Al-Wateen), and no force on Earth could protect him. This establishes an absolute theological law: no human being has the right to manipulate divine truth to suit personal agendas or societal trends. The truth belongs to God alone.
The Surah closes by describing the Quran as Haqqul-Yaqeen - the highest level of certainty. Truth ignored today does not cease to be true; it simply transforms into regret (Hasrah) tomorrow. The ultimate response to this reality is given in the final verse: Tasbeeh - glorifying the Name of Allah, the Most Great, acknowledging His perfect wisdom, authority, and divine design.

stories_in_surah.title: Divine Vindication of the Qur'an and Prophetic Integrity (Verses 38-52)
stories_in_surah.content:
The concluding section addresses the slander cast by Makkan opponents who claimed Muhammad (pbuh) was a poet (Sha'ir) or a fortune-teller/soothsayer (Kahin).

Divine Oaths (Verses 38-40)

Allah swears by a grand cosmic oath:

• "So I swear by what you see and what you do not see, [that] indeed, the Qur'an is the word of a noble Messenger."* (Verses 38-40)

By swearing by the visible universe and the invisible unseen realm, Allah encompasses all of creation to guarantee the authenticity of the Revelation.

Refutation of Slander (Verses 41-43)

• Not Poetry: "And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe."
• Not Soothsaying: "Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember."
• The True Source: "It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds."

The Safeguard of Prophetic Honesty (Verses 44-47)

Allah delivers one of the most severe warnings in scripture regarding the absolute preservation of Divine Revelation:

• "And if he [Muhammad] had made up about Us some [false] sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand; then We would have cut from him the aorta (Al-Wateen). And there is no one of you who could prevent Us from him."* (Verses 44-47)

Theological Significance

This passage establishes the complete honesty and integrity of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Had the Prophet (pbuh) added or altered a single word of divine revelation for personal or political gain, divine retribution would have been immediate and fatal. This reassures humanity that the Qur'an remains 100% unadulterated divine speech.

Conclusion and Final Mandate (Verses 48-52)

The Surah concludes by summarizing the nature of the Qur'an:

1. A Reminder for the Righteous: "And indeed, the Qur'an is a reminder for the righteous" (Verse 48).
2. A Cause of Regret for Disbelievers: Rejection of truth will turn into profound regret (Hasrah) on Judgment Day (Verse 50).
3. Indisputable Truth: It is the absolute, certain truth (Haqq al-Yaqin) (Verse 51).

The Final Command (Verse 52)

• "So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great (Fasabbih bismi rabbika al-'Azeem).

deep_dives.title: Historical Retribution: Lessons from Past Nations (Verses 4-12)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah establishes the reality of future judgment by presenting historical evidence: nations that rejected their Prophets and denied the Day of Reckoning (Al-Qari'ah) were swiftly wiped out in this life.

1. Thamud (Verse 5)

• The Transgression: Defied Prophet Salih (as) and slaughtered the divine She-Camel.
• The Punishment: Destroyed by At-Taghiyah - an overwhelming, deafening soundwave and earthquake that exceeded all human endurance.

2. 'Ad (Verses 6-8)

• The Transgression: Proud of their physical stature and power, they rejected Prophet Hud (as).
• The Punishment: Wiped out by Rihin sarsarin 'atiyah - a furious, ice-cold, roaring wind storm that Allah imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days continuously.
• The Visual Metaphor: Verse 7 describes their fallen corpses scattered across the valley like "hollow trunks of palm trees." Verse 8 poses a haunting rhetorical question: "Do you see of them any remains?"

3. Pharaoh, His Predecessors, and the Overturned Cities (Verses 9-10)

• The Transgression: Persistent sinfulness, political tyranny, and social corruption (referring to Pharaoh and the people of Sodom/Gomorrah associated with Prophet Lut, as).
• The Punishment: Taken by an overflowing, increasing grip of punishment (Akhdhatan rabiyah).

4. The Ark of Noah (Verses 11-12)

• Divine Mercy in Calamity: When the waters transgressed their bounds, Allah carried humanity's ancestors in the floating Ark (Al-Jariyah).
• Purpose of History: Verse 12 clarifies why these accounts are preserved: "That We might make it for you a reminder and that an attentive ear (Udhunun wa'iyah) might conscious it.

deep_dives.title: The Mechanics of Resurrection and Judgment Day (Verses 13-18)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah shifts from past history to the future cosmic dismantling of the cosmos.

Cosmic Dismantling (Verses 13-16)

1. The Single Blast: A single blow on the Trumpet (Nafkhatun wahidah) initiates the end of earthly existence.
2. Destruction of the Earth and Mountains: The earth and mountains will be lifted and crushed with a single impact (Dakkatan wahidah).
3. Frail Sky: The sky will split apart, becoming structurally weak, torn, and fragile on that Day.

The Eight Bearers of the Throne (Verse 17)

Allah describes the angelic order on that terrifying Day:

• "And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them, that Day, eight [angels]."* (Verse 17)

Authentic Hadith Context

Regarding the immense grandeur of these angels carrying the Divine Throne ('Arsh), Jabir ibn 'Abdillah (ra) reported that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said in Sunan Abi Dawud (Hadith 4727):

• "I have been permitted to speak about one of the angels of Allah from among the bearers of the Throne. Indeed, the distance between his earlobe and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years."

Absolute Transparency (Verse 18)

• "That Day, you will be exhibited [for judgment]; not hidden among you is the slightest secret."*

Every motive, action, and private thought will be exposed before the Creator.

deep_dives.title: The Two Books of Deeds: Contrast of Destinies (Verses 19-37)
deep_dives.content:
The middle section presents a dramatic contrast between the two possible outcomes of human life, depicted through the physical reception of the Book of Deeds (Kitab).

The Right Hand: The Triumphant Believer (Verses 19-24)

• Ecstatic Joy: The person who receives their book in their right hand shouts out in jubilation to the gathered assembly: "Here, read my record!" (Ha'umu qra'u kitabiyah).
• The Mindset: They lived with active accountability: "Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account" (Verse 20).
• The Reward: A pleasant life in an elevated Paradise (Jannatin 'aliyah), whose clusters of fruit hang within easy reach (Qutufuha daniyah), invited to eat and drink in satisfaction for what they sent ahead in past days.

The Left Hand: The Ruined Transgressor (Verses 25-37)

• Utter Despair: The person given their record in their left hand cries out in agony: "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record and had never known what is my account! Oh, I wish my death had been the end!" (Verses 25-27).
• Loss of Power: They realize the illusion of material power: "My wealth has not availed me; gone from me is my authority" (Verses 28-29).

Divine Sentence and Character Breakdown (Verses 30-37)

The divine command goes forth: "Seize him and shackle him, then drive him into Hellfire, then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him."

Allah isolates the two foundational moral failures that led to this ruin:

1. Failure in Faith: "Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Most Great" (Verse 33).
2. Failure in Social Compassion: "Nor did he encourage the feeding of the poor" (Verse 34).

Because he showed no empathy or aid to vulnerable human beings in the world, he finds no close friend (Hamim) on Judgment Day, and his food is only Ghislin (a foul discharge from the inhabitants of the Fire).
